question_title: Thunderbird cannot send emails from multiple accounts – SMTP timeouts and OAuth2 issues
question_content: Hello Thunderbird Support Team, I am experiencing serious email problems with Thunderbird on two Windows 11 computers. I use Thunderbird for approximately 12–13 email accounts, mostly Gmail accounts, for my accounting work.  The main problem:**   Thunderbird receives incoming emails, but I cannot send messages from multiple accounts. On the first computer, Thunderbird displays the following error: "Sending of the message failed. The connection to the outgoing server (SMTP) smtp.gmail.com timed out." On the second computer, Thunderbird repeatedly asks me to authenticate my Gmail accounts again. The authentication process does not seem to resolve the sending issue.  What I have already checked:**   - Thunderbird version: 153.6.0 ESR on the first computer. - SMTP server: smtp.gmail.com. - Port 465 with SSL/TLS and OAuth2. - Tested port 587 with STARTTLS – same problem. - Thunderbird successfully establishes a secure connection to smtp.gmail.com:465, but sending emails still fails. - Cookies, including third-party cookies, are enabled. - Tested Thunderbird Troubleshoot Mode. - Restarted Thunderbird and Windows. - The problem occurs on two different computers and different Wi-Fi networks. - Gmail accounts work through the web browser.  Additional information:**   The problems initially appeared when one Gmail account stopped synchronizing. I removed that account from Thunderbird, but its IMAP server configuration remained in the Thunderbird profile (prefs.js). I subsequently experienced sending problems with other accounts. I found Bugzilla report 2062925, which appears to describe similar problems involving multiple Gmail accounts and SMTP timeouts.  My questions:**   1. Is this a known issue in Thunderbird 153 ESR? 2. Could a malfunctioning Gmail account or an orphaned IMAP configuration interfere with SMTP sending from other accounts? 3. Is there an official fix or workaround that does not require deleting and reconfiguring all accounts? 4. Could Google OAuth2 authentication or Google Contacts synchronization be responsible? I would appreciate your help. I rely on Thunderbird for my daily accounting work, and I cannot currently send emails reliably. Thank you in advance.
